entries.summary: Never narrate an action as underway without the tool call in the same turn
entries.problem: Ended a message with 'polling for that pass now' without starting any poll. The user had to notice and ask. This is worse than a wrong fact: a wrong fact can be checked against the code, but a claimed action is invisible until someone independently discovers nothing happened — and in the meantime they are waiting on work that does not exist. The same shape covers 'kicking off X', 'running Y in the background', 'watching for Z', and 'I'll monitor that' when no monitor, background command, or scheduled wakeup was created.
entries.solution: Before writing that an action is in progress, confirm the tool call for it appears in the same turn. If it does not, either make the call or change the tense: 'I'll poll next' is honest, 'polling now' is a claim. Present-progressive and 'now' are the tells. For anything asynchronous — background commands, monitors, subagents, scheduled wakeups — the claim is only true if a tool call returned an id or handle; quote or act on that handle rather than asserting the work is running.

entries.summary: Judge a verification gate by its exit code, never by grepping its output

entries.summary: Verify base branch is synced with remote before creating a PR
entries.problem: If the local base branch has commits that were never pushed, GitHub compares the PR branch against the remote state of the base — making all unpushed commits appear as new. This caused a PR to show the entire repo as changed (85 background commits from a local feat/memtree-v1 that was never pushed before branching).
entries.solution:
Before running `gh pr create`, verify the local base is in sync with remote:
git fetch origin
git log origin/<BASE>..<BASE> --oneline   # must be empty
git log <BASE>..origin/<BASE> --oneline   # must be empty
git log origin/<BASE>..HEAD --oneline | wc -l  # should equal expected commit count

If local base is ahead of remote, push it first.

entries.summary: A paginated query returning exactly the page size is truncated, not counted
entries.problem: Queried GitHub review threads with `reviewThreads(first: 100)` and never followed `pageInfo.endCursor`, then reported 'zero unresolved threads' from the result. The real totals were 126 threads and 27 unresolved — every one of them unanswered. The tell was in the output the whole time: total read exactly 100, the page size. A round number equal to the limit is a truncation signal, not a measurement. The runbook being followed explicitly said to paginate and follow the cursor; the query was written from memory instead. This produced a confident false 'all clear' on a merge gate, twice.
entries.solution: Any paginated API read that feeds a decision must follow the cursor to exhaustion, or explicitly report that it is a partial page. Check `pageInfo.hasNextPage` and loop on `endCursor` — never infer completeness from the node count. Treat a result whose length equals the requested `first`/`per_page` as presumptively truncated. For REST, use `--paginate`. The same rule covers `gh api` list endpoints, search results, and any 'first N' query: if the count could gate an action, it must be the whole set.

entries.summary: Never let code inherit the interactive model when spawning an LLM subprocess
entries.problem: Code that shells out to an LLM CLI without an explicit model argument inherits whatever the user's interactive default is. A summarize-to-JSON enrichment pass inherited Opus and ran 2,825 times in 43 hours, costing roughly 20x what the task needed and consuming about 69% of a weekly quota. The task was small-model work throughout; nothing in the code expressed that intent.
entries.solution:
Always pass all three isolation flags when spawning a claude -p subprocess — omitting any one of them leaves a vector open:

  claude -p "<prompt>" \
    --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 \
    --no-session-persistence \
    --setting-sources ""

• --model: pins the model so the subprocess cannot inherit whatever the interactive session is using. Choose haiku for extraction/summarization (economy) and sonnet for code tasks (accuracy). Never omit and rely on the caller to have set a default.
• --no-session-persistence: prevents the subprocess from writing a new session file, so repeated invocations do not accumulate ghost sessions.
• --setting-sources "": disables all hooks and plugin loading in the subprocess. A bare claude -p inherits every hook the parent session has, which can re-trigger the calling hook recursively and emit thousands of ghost sessions (PM-005: 36,468 ghost sessions from one Stop hook).

Make the model overridable by env var and resolve the override per call, not at module load. Guard blank overrides: a null-coalescing ?? catches undefined but passes through an empty string, which fails the --model flag silently.
